title: Frequency-adapted endpoint shell and resolvent-compatible filter
question: Can an energy-difference filter F_s(u)=(1+u)^(-s) suppress the cutoff-sensitive endpoint shell while retaining a finite bridge that is compatible with the R-377 resolvent?

identity.resolvent_role: The filter is a finite spectral analogue of energy/resolvent smoothing; removing it uniformly is a separate open approximation gate.

promotion_boundary: R-383 is a finite spectral-filter diagnostic. It can show whether resolvent-compatible energy weighting suppresses the R-382 cutoff growth, but it does not prove filter removal, a common core, a thermodynamic limit, or a QFT theorem.
next_action: Prove a uniform filter-removal estimate on the Hamiltonian-derived common core, or register a precise obstruction if the filtered-to-raw approximation fails; then connect the filtered endpoint shell to the R-377 resolvent telescope.
boundary: Finite actual-Q3 edge d=3,4,5,6 and square d=2 doubled-bond matrices with all declared histories. Filtered endpoint/M0/M2 envelopes, profiles, and independent agreement are checked numerically and in Lean; source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, filter removal, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
